item: the CSRF guard compares the Origin's host and effective port with the Host header's (audit A-001, A-017)
summary: The guard compared only the Origin's hostname with the loopback names, so any other local web app (Origin http://localhost:9999) passed, and a JSON route reached with an untyped body needed no preflight. The Origin (or the Referer when no Origin is sent) must now name the same hostname and the same effective port (80/443 by scheme) as the Host header, the hostname being one the Host guard serves, so OO_ALLOWED_HOSTS names work for a self-hoster's own UI (A-017, documented in SECURITY.md). A non-http(s) scheme or a port that is not a number is refused. 13 red-without tests incl. Referer-only and a no-Content-Type body to /api/system/network. Not browser-verified; the content-type middleware stays a separate defence in depth.
